item.title: Korea Square draws 26,000 visitors in Hong Kong over 2 days
item.description: A two-day celebration of Korean culture has drawn approximately 26,000 visitors in Hong Kong, nearly tripling last year's attendance and bringing Korean companies, local creators and public institutions together under one roof. Korea Square 2026, organized by the Korean Cultural Center in Hong Kong, took place Saturday and Sunday at PMQ's Courtyard & Marketplace and QUBE performance venue, transforming the central Hong Kong cultural complex into a showcase for Korean food, beauty, music, entertainment and design. Now in its sixth year, the festival attracted roughly three times the 9,000 visitors recorded last year, reflecting growing local interest in Korean culture, according to the center. More than 50 Korean companies, Hong Kong-based brands, creators and public institutions participated, including Samsung, LG and mobile game developer Com2uS, alongside the Korea Tourism Organization, Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, Korea Agro-Fisheries and Food Trade Corp. and the Korea Creative Content Agency. item.title: Hyundai, Kia win int'l certification for in-house chip development process
item.description: Hyundai Motor and Kia have received international certification for the process they use to develop their own automotive semiconductors, the companies said Thursday. The carmakers held a ceremony Wednesday at Pangyo Tech One, their office complex in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, a tech hub just south of Seoul, to receive the certification from TUV Rheinland, a German testing and certification company. It confirms that their chip development process and functional safety management system comply with an international standard based on the rules of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). Functional safety refers to designing electronic systems so that a vehicle stays safe even when a component fails. Since 2025, the two automakers have run their own standard process tailored to developing automotive system-on-chip products, semiconductors that integrate multiple functions on a single chip. item.title: KT launches AI portal to help businesses navigate digital transformation
item.description: KT launched an online consulting platform designed to help businesses move from artificial intelligence ambitions (AI) to practical implementation, offering tailored technology recommendations, industry strategies and access to experts. The telecommunications company said Thursday it had opened the KT AX Biz Portal, a specialized platform that brings together information and services for companies exploring AI transformation (AX). item.title: Myeong-dong shops turn trash disposal into unexpected act of hospitality for tourists
item.description: Tourists wandering through Myeong-dong can now enjoy street food and drinks without worrying about where to throw away their trash, thanks to an unusual initiative that turns local vendors into volunteer waste collectors. The Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Seoul Tourism Organization have launched a promotional campaign encouraging visitors to hand empty drink cups and food packaging to participating street vendors, who will dispose of the waste on their behalf. A total of 346 street stalls in Myeong-dong are taking part in the Clean Myeong-dong campaign, which aims to improve tourist convenience while keeping one of Seoul's busiest shopping districts clean. The initiative grew out of complaints from visitors who struggled to find trash bins after buying food and beverages from street stalls. It was developed following a request from Seoul Namdaemun Police Station, with local vendors voluntarily joining the effort. item.title: Nexen Tire expands winter lineup with new model optimized for ice
item.description: Nexen Tire is expanding its winter tire lineup with a new model designed specifically for icy roads, targeting drivers who face treacherous conditions during early-morning and nighttime travel. The company said Wednesday it had launched the Winguard ice3 in Korea, adding an ice-focused option to its existing winter tire offerings. The new tire has earned the Ice Grip marking, a certification awarded to products that meet braking performance standards on icy surfaces. It is designed to maintain flexibility and traction in low temperatures through a specialized rubber compound, while its wider tread profile increases contact with the road. The product is aimed particularly at motorists who frequently drive through areas prone to icy conditions or travel during hours when temperatures are low and roads are more likely to freeze. With the launch, Nexen Tire now offers three winter tire options: the Winguard ice3, Winguard Sport 2 and Winguard Sport 2 SUV. The product is aimed particularly at motorists who frequently drive through areas prone to icy conditions or travel during hours when temperatures are low and roads are more likely to freeze. item.title: Lee welcomes East Timor President Horta's visit to Korea ahead of summit
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday welcomed East Timorese President Jose Ramos-Horta's first visit to Korea, expressing hope for a stronger partnership between the two countries on the occasion of next year's 25th anniversary of diplomatic relations. Lee wrote the message on his X account, as Horta was scheduled to make an official visit to Korea from Thursday through Saturday, marking the first trip to Korea by an East Timorese leader since the two countries established diplomatic relations in 2002. item.title: Why are Chinese consumers tuning out of annual online shopping festival?
item.description: Hangzhou bank employee Xiao Na says she has no plan to buy anything during China’s ongoing Singles’ Day shopping festival, the world’s largest online retail promotion. “When I think about hunting around for things to buy just so I can use all kinds of coupons, the money I save is dwarfed by what I’ve lost in the stock market,” the 37-year-old said. “Stocks are falling, home values continue to slide, and my salary isn’t going up. Keeping more cash in my pocket is the best strategy.” Consumers across China are holding back on spending during the annual shopping extravaganza as a stock market slump and a prolonged decline in property values erode household wealth, with many families making debt reduction and deleveraging greater priorities. In the third quarter, the tech-focused ChiNext Index plunged nearly 28 percent — one of its steepest quarterly declines on record — while the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index posted more moderate losses amid a sharp unwinding in growth and technology stocks. item.title: Korea, Singapore, New Zealand review progress in green trade pact talks
item.description: Korea, Singapore and New Zealand have discussed progress in negotiations and key outstanding issues related to their trilateral Green Economy Partnership Agreement (GEPA), the industry ministry said Thursday. Senior officials from the three countries held a videoconference ahead of the APEC Economic Leaders' Week, scheduled to begin next week in China, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. Through the agreement, Seoul seeks to work with the two partners to jointly address the challenges posed by trade-related climate measures (TrCMs), including the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and help businesses maintain stable operations amid an increasingly volatile global trade environment, the ministry said. CBAM is an EU policy instrument designed to ensure that imported goods face a carbon price comparable to that imposed on products manufactured within the bloc. item.title: Hanwha Aerospace breaks ground on Chunmoo rocket plant in Poland
item.description: Hanwha Aerospace said Thursday it has broken ground on a guided rocket manufacturing plant in Poland as part of efforts to expand its defense production capabilities in Europe. The Korean defense company held a groundbreaking ceremony Wednesday (local time) in Gorzow Wielkopolski, western Poland, alongside Hanwha WB Advanced Systems (HWBAS), its joint venture with Poland's WB Group. The plant, scheduled for completion in 2028, will mark Hanwha Aerospace's first guided weapons production facility in Europe. The facility will manufacture CGR-080 guided rockets for the HOMAR-K, the Polish version of Hanwha's Chunmoo multiple rocket launcher system (MLRS). The company plans to roll out the first batch in late 2029 before beginning full-scale production in 2030. HWBAS was established in September 2025, with Hanwha Aerospace holding a 51 percent stake and Poland's WB Electronics owning the remaining 49 percent. The joint venture has signed a contract with Poland's Armament Agency to produce and supply CGR-080 guided rockets, with Hanwha Aerospace set to transfer manufacturing technology to HWBAS

item.title: Korea's stock markets to open 1 hour later Nov. 19
item.description: Korea's stock markets will start trading an hour later than usual on Nov. 19 due to the nationwide college entrance exam, the bourse operator said Thursday. Trading on the main KOSPI and secondary KOSDAQ stock markets will begin at 10 a.m. and close at 4:30 p.m., the Korea Exchange (KRX) said in a statement. On Nov. 19, an after-market trading session will also begin at 5 p.m., an hour later than usual, and close at 8 p.m., the KRX said. More than 551,000 high school seniors and graduates will take the one-day standardized College Scholastic Ability Test, according to the education ministry.

item.title: West Point cadet drugged girlfriend to force unwanted abortion: lawsuit
item.description: NEW YORK — A onetime West Point cadet drugged his then-girlfriend in her barracks room, administered abortion pills to her against her will and caused a miscarriage. Then he went on to study at two Ivy League universities, starting at one of them after he pleaded guilty to assault, according to court records and a new lawsuit. The man, Caleb Suh, graduated from Cornell University this year and was a public health graduate student at Columbia University as of Oct. 28, when the woman sued in a New York court. His current status at Columbia is unclear. The suit drew attention to a case that had played out quietly at West Point and in federal court, where Suh pleaded guilty this past June to the March 2022 assault on a cadet in the class below him. She was 19 and in her second year at the U.S. Military Academy, according to prosecutors. She wanted to have the baby. Suh didn't. item.title: Jung Woo-sung cast in upcoming Joseon-era action film
item.description: Actor Jung Woo-sung has been cast as a powerful politician of the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) in the upcoming Korean film "The Hit List," its production companies said Thursday. The film portrays cold-blooded politician Han Myeong-hoe (Jung), a key aide to King Sejo, who rises to power through his ruthless tactics but comes to face people seeking revenge after losing everything to him, according to Cheum Film and Studio Take. The film, which the production companies called "a hard-boiled, action-packed historical film," is based on a webtoon of the same name. Alongside Jung, its cast also includes actors Jung Sung-il, Baek Yun-shik, Wi Ha-joon and Choi Daniel. Kim Hong-seon, known for "Traffickers" (2012) and "Project Wolf Hunting" (2022), is the director. International crew members took part in the production, including Lars Cox, a cinematographer on HBO's "House of the Dragon," and Kieran Waite, a lighting director who worked on the epic "The Odyssey."

item.title: KRX activates sell-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp fall
item.description: Korea's bourse operator on Thursday activated a sell-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the stock index plunged. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes at 10:16 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). After opening 1.82 percent lower, the KOSPI surrendered 265.65 points, or 4.67 percent, to 5,418.15 as of 10:16 a.m. The index came under downward pressure following the Democratic Party's victory in the U.S. midterm elections, raising concerns over tighter regulations on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. A sell-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index falls 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

item.title: Over 470,000 pieces of personal data leaked from 37 financial firms: FSC
item.description: More than 470,000 personal data records have been leaked from 37 companies across the financial sector over the past month, with the amount of funds stolen estimated at 1 billion won ($745,000), the financial regulator said Thursday. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) held a meeting with officials from financial trade associations and government agencies, including the Financial Supervisory Service and the Financial Security Institute, to review data protection systems and artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities in the financial sector. Since Sept. 30, when the first data leak was detected, a total of 40 data leak incidents have been reported at 37 companies, including four commercial banks, five financial investment firms, three insurance firms and five savings banks, according to the FSC. The regulator said the leaked data did not include sensitive personal information that could be used for illegal financial transactions, such as customers' names, national identification numbers or bank account numbers. item.title: Trump says Hegseth doing 'a very good job' as questions swirl about his future
item.description: WASHINGTON — US President Donald Trump backed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday, a day after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in midterm elections that reflected voter anger over the Iran war. Asked whether he was considering replacing Hegseth, whom he has described as a champion of the war, Trump told reporters: "No, I think he's doing a very good job." The response contrasted with then-President George Bush, who fired Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld the morning after the 2006 midterm elections, when voter discontent over the Iraq war helped Democrats win control of Congress. But sources said Trump could still replace Hegseth as Republicans assess their losses. One Trump adviser said Hegseth "could be on the chopping block" because of the war. "Someone is going to get blamed for this and you know it's not going to be him (Trump)," the adviser said. The seven-member group under SM Entertainment will release “DREAM AFTER DREAM,” featuring 10 tracks across various genres, on global music platforms at 6 p.m. Monday. “Boogie Woogie” blends the nostalgic sound of 1970s disco funk with modern synthesizers in an upbeat dance track that celebrates the group's 10 years together. The song carries a message of gratitude toward those who have made everyday moments special, encouraging listeners to appreciate the present and enjoy life together. item.title: TXT previews new album with 6 tracks capturing turbulence of youth
item.description: K-pop group Tomorrow X Together, better known as TXT, gave global fans a first taste of their upcoming album, teasing six new tracks that channel the raw friction, desires and restless intensity of young adulthood through a genre-spanning soundscape. The five-member group released the preview video for its ninth mini album, “PERFECT STORM,” on HYBE Labels' YouTube channel at midnight Wednesday. The preview features snippets of all six tracks, including lead single “Angel Bite,” alongside “Storm is...,” “Higher Love,” “Sweetest Escape,” “Touch the Sky” and “Hate It or Love It.” The album examines the struggles of Generation Z as its members move beyond teenage fantasies and uncertainty to confront adult realities, according to BigHit Music. Its title track, “Angel Bite,” blends playful, video game-inspired sounds with rough-edged yet wistful melodies in a style described as disco-plug. item.title: S. Korea rejects Russia's criticism of joint military exercises with US
item.description: South Korea on Thursday rejected Russia's criticism of its joint military exercises with the United States, stressing that the drills are defensive in nature and aimed at promoting peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula. Seoul's foreign ministry issued the statement after a spokesperson at Russia's foreign ministry claimed Tuesday the South Korea-U.S. exercises are designed "to rehearse preemptive strikes" against North Korea, including with nuclear weapons, and urged Seoul "to respect Pyongyang's sovereign right" to ensure its own security. "The joint South Korea-U.S. military exercises are defensive in nature and are conducted annually to maintain a robust combined defense posture in response to North Korea's advancing nuclear and missile threats," Seoul's foreign ministry said in a statement sent to Yonhap News Agency. "They contribute to peace and stability not only on the Korean Peninsula but also in Northeast Asia," it added. item.title: Shin Min-a, Lee Jin-uk to appear in upcoming romance drama
item.description: Actors Shin Min-a and Lee Jin-uk will portray a couple who reunite after a breakup in an upcoming romance drama set to premiere in the first half of next year, its broadcaster said Thursday. Set in a restaurant that only opens Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, the series follows the love, forgiveness and growth of its lead characters, according to MBC. The Korean title of the series is "Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays." Shin portrays Eun-soo, who reunites with a boyfriend she broke up with 12 years ago, while Lee appears as the chef of the restaurant and Eun-soo's former boyfriend. The series also features Teo Yoo as Eun-soo's husband, a business executive. Joo Hyun, known for "The World of the Married," based on the BBC series "Doctor Foster," penned the upcoming drama, while director Jung Dong-yoon of the sports drama "Stove League" helmed the series.

item.description: Stray Kids has added another milestone in Japan, earning the group's third streaming platinum certification as the group prepares to launch three nights of concerts at Tokyo Dome on Friday. “Special,” the lead track of the group's third full-length album, “★★★★★ (5-STAR),” surpassed 100 million cumulative streams in Japan as of September 2026, earning platinum certification from the Recording Industry Association of Japan, according to JYP Entertainment. item.title: SK Biopharm's Q3 operating profit up 66% on US sales of seizure drug
item.description: SK Biopharmaceuticals, a biopharmaceutical arm of SK Group, said Thursday its operating profit rose 65.9 percent from a year earlier, boosted by robust U.S. sales of oral anti-seizure medication. The company reported an operating profit of 116.3 billion won in the July-September period, according to its regulatory filing. Sales increased 34.8 percent to 258.4 billion won. But net income was down 23.9 percent to 54.3 billion won. The sharp rise in operating profit came despite adjustments to the won-dollar exchange, helped by the robust growth of its seizure drug, Cenobamate, also known as Xcopri in the United States, the company said. The strengthening of the won also helped lower costs, it added. The sales generated in the U.S. from the oral prescription drug came to $156.8 million, up 29.9 percent on-year, the company said. item.title: Seoul shares sharply down late Thursday morning as US midterm results spark AI woes
item.description: South Korean stocks traded sharply lower late Thursday morning as investors were worried about the future of U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) policies after the midterm elections. After opening 1.82 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) extended losses, dropping 185.77 points, or 3.27 percent, to 5,498.03 as of 11:20 a.m. Overnight on Wall Street, major stock indexes finished higher as investors welcomed the Democrats-led Congress. However, the election outcome raised concerns that the new House and Senate would tighten regulations on AI data centers. In Seoul, semiconductor shares traded in negative territory. Tech giant Samsung Electronics sank 5.05 percent, and SK hynix tumbled 6.52 percent. Hanmi Semiconductor, a leading chip equipment maker, plunged 7.58 percent, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, the electronic component affiliate of Samsung Electronics, dived 10.04 percent. Leading oil refinery SK Innovation lost 5.9 percent, and defense giant Hanwha Aerospace fell 4.76 percent. The Korean won was trading at 1,342.15 won against the U.S. dollar as of 11:2

item.title: [COVER STORY] Seoul to send anti-piracy unit closer to Hormuz, add mine-clearing team
item.description: The government decided Thursday to expand the mission of its anti-piracy Cheonghae Unit closer to the Strait of Hormuz, extending its operating area from the Gulf of Aden to waters south of Oman and adding military assets to protect shipping routes. The move is sparking concerns that it could draw Korea into the war between Iran and the United States. The expansion proposal passed a vice ministerial meeting Thursday morning. After Cabinet and presidential approval, the motion will go to the National Assembly for final authorization. Under the proposal, the unit’s personnel ceiling would rise from 320 to 395, with the addition of a P-8 maritime patrol aircraft, an explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) team and unmanned mine-clearing equipment. The additional 75 personnel would include 45 assigned to the P-8 aircraft and 30 to the EOD team. The new equipment would include unmanned surface and underwater vehicles and remotely operated underwater robots. The revised mandate would also add support for restoring freedom of navigation along international shipping routes to the unit’s existing an

item.title: French blood banks face cyberattack, no blood damaged
item.description: France's national blood service suffered a cyberattack on its refrigeration systems, in an apparent escalation of attacks on European refrigerators and freezers. The French blood service EFS said the temperature thresholds were raised "to very high levels" in the attack, but no blood or blood products were ruined, thanks to alarm systems. Products stored in the affected rooms were moved to other sites. The EFS collects, tests, prepares and distributes products such as blood, plasma and platelets to more than 1,900 hospitals in France. It supports more than a million patients per year. The attack mirrors those on grocery stores in 12 countries recently that caused millions of euros in food loss. Some systems' temperatures were raised to 122 degrees Fahrenheit. On Monday, systems in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden reported issues, and on Tuesday, retailers in Italy, Germany, Romania and Britain were targeted. item.title: Democratic Congress could test decades of US support for Israel
item.description: WASHINGTON — Democrats’ takeover of Congress and growing Republican unease over Israel could trigger the biggest reassessment of US support for its closest Middle East ally in decades, after an election shaped in part by anger over the Iran war. Democrats won both the Senate and House in Tuesday’s midterms. Many winning candidates were progressives who campaigned against military aid to Israel and the US-Israeli war on Iran. Israel’s campaign in Gaza and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s embrace of President Donald Trump and other Republicans had already strained decades of bipartisan support for Israel. Democratic control could bring greater scrutiny of military aid and West Bank violence, along with hearings and challenges to Trump nominees, although the president’s veto limits the party’s ability to force major policy changes. One successful progressive was Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, the first Muslim elected to the US Senate despite Republican attempts to win over Jewish voters who might have been uncomfortable with his faith and his criticism of Israel. item.title: Kakao Q3 operating profit up 15.5% on stable growth of platform biz
item.description: Korean internet tech giant Kakao Corp. said Thursday its operating profit rose 15.5 percent from a year earlier, boosted by the stable growth of its flagship platform business. On a consolidated basis, the company reported an operating profit of 240.3 billion won ($179.2 million) in the July-September period, according to its regulatory filing. Sales remained unchanged at 2.08 trillion won, while net income was down 7.9 percent to 177.7 billion won. The company's flagship platform business saw sales grow 17 percent on-year to 1.24 trillion won. Notably, turnover of its commerce business rose 13 percent on-year to 2.3 trillion won, as more people used the KakaoTalk platform to purchase goods during the Chuseok holiday and as well as to buy items for themselves, the IT company explained. Kakao's ride-hailing and payment services, also included in its platform unit, generated 602.1 billion won in sales, up 21 percent on-year. But sales from its content business were down 6 percent on-year to 851.7 billion won due to a drop in new album releases and large concerts, as well as a decline in sale

item.title: Korea posts record high current account surplus of over $60 bil. in Sept. on chip supercycle
item.description: Korea posted an all-time high current account surplus of over $60 billion in September on strong exports of semiconductors, central bank data showed Thursday. The current account surplus totaled $61.46 billion in September, up from $46.11 billion the previous month, according to the data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). It marked the largest monthly current account surplus ever, renewing the previous record of $49.73 billion set in June. Compared with the same month a year earlier, the figure surged from $14.22 billion. For the first nine months of the year, the current account surplus totaled a cumulative $340.66 billion, quadrupling from $83.89 billion recorded over the same period last year. The third-quarter current account surplus totaled $149.65 billion, already surpassing last year's annual total of $123.05 billion. The BOK expected this year's annual current account surplus to exceed its forecast of $450 billion. item.title: N. Korea says test-fired new air defense missile system, long-range cruise missile
item.description: North Korea has test-fired a new air defense missile system and conducted a strike drill with a long-range strategic cruise missile, state media reported Thursday, marking Pyongyang's fourth weapons test in a week. The North's report came after South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) detected the North firing multiple missiles toward the East Sea from the Sondok area in South Hamgyong Province early Wednesday. The Missile Administration's test of a new air defense missile system was aimed at confirming its technical capabilities, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). item.title: Elon Musk's business empire braces for Democratic wave as Texas flips blue
item.description: As Republicans suffered a landslide defeat and Texas elected its first Democratic governor in more than three decades, one of the biggest losers of the US midterms was not on the ballot: billionaire Elon Musk. The world's richest man spent nearly half a billion dollars to back Republican candidates and keep Texas red - a state home to his automaker Tesla, rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two. Those bets unraveled as Democrats seized both chambers of Congress and Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, in a stinging rebuke to US President Donald Trump, a close Musk ally whom the billionaire helped elect. Musk, who urged his followers on X to vote Republican as recently as Tuesday, now faces a resurgent Democratic Party that he has spent years antagonizing. The GOP's largest donor even threatened retaliation last month on his social media platform after a report said Democrats were considering probes into his companies if they won midterms. item.title: UNESCO likely to list traditional Korean paper 'hanji' as cultural heritage
item.description: The knowledge and skills associated with the production of "hanji," or traditional Korean paper, are likely to be added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage. In a document released Wednesday (France time), UNESCO said its deliberative body has categorized "traditional knowledge and skills associated with the production of hanji, traditional Korean paper, and related cultural practices in the Republic of Korea" as recommended for inscription. The Republic of Korea is South Korea's official name. "Hanji plays an important role in the daily life and cultural practices of the communities concerned, as it is widely used for writing, printing, crafts, household and ritual objects," it said. The tradition of hanji, paper made from the bark of mulberry trees, runs for about a thousand years, and the meticulous handcrafting skills of hanji masters have been passed down through generations. item.title: [ROUNDTABLE] Korea needs AI-ready ontology, should not end with developing models
item.description: Korea needs to diversify its current artificial intelligence (AI) strategy which is largely confined to developing advanced models, and expand its efforts to build AI-ready knowledge systems, infrastructure and a regulatory environment that supports practical applications, experts said during The Korea Times roundtable, “Beyond US-China AI race: Korea's strategic edge.” The participants called for greater efforts to build ontologies — structured knowledge systems that organize vast amounts of government data, institutional knowledge and the relationships between them into forms AI systems can understand and use. They also agreed to the necessity of creating a sandbox area where AI-powered technologies could be tested and deployed under a more flexible regulatory framework. Reform Party of Korea Rep. item.title: AI movies make leap from short clips to big screen
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) technology is expanding its reach from short online videos to feature-length films as another fully generated movie heads to local theaters. The shift comes as industry experts say that cinema is entering a transition period where AI tools are rapidly pushing moviemakers to figure out how and where to use the technology. At the same time, growing fears over creator rights have sparked heated debate across the industry. Previous AI releases have also shown that technical novelty on its own does not translate into box office success. "Raphael," a science fiction movie created entirely using generative AI, will open on Nov. 25. Set in a post-apocalyptic future, the movie follows Alexey, an android weapon built in the image of a dictator, who discovers his humanity after meeting an unregistered child and the last human bride. Co-directed by Yang Ik-june, Moon Shin-woo and Jung Joo-won, the movie is produced by Mateo AI Studio and MBC C&I AI Content Lab. The team used generative AI to build characters and backgrounds and create massive war scenes without tradition

item.title: Trump says 'largely true' Iran war caused midterms loss
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday acknowledged that the Iran war was the key factor in his party's sweeping midterm election losses, after Vice President JD Vance urged Republicans to be "honest" about the unpopular conflict's impact. Asked if he agreed with Vance's remark that the Iran was "the reason we lost," Trump, speaking to reporters at his White House ballroom construction site, said: "I think it's largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term." "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he added

item.title: Voters in US capital say 'oui' to foie gras ban
item.description: WASHINGTON — The production and sale of foie gras is set to become illegal in Washington after voters in the U.S. capital overwhelmingly backed a measure banning the controversial gourmet food item. The ban however could face possible delays or be overturned, with media reports saying foie gras producers and restaurants are likely to challenge it in court. Initiative 86, as the referendum is known, won 73 percent of the vote on Tuesday, according to provisional results. It bars the force-feeding of birds to enlarge their livers as well as the sale of any product resulting from the practice. Activists say that the production of foie gras is torturous to ducks and geese. Washington currently has no farms or facilities producing the classic French delicacy, but restaurants that serve it could face fines of $1,000 to $5,000 as well as a suspension of their operating license. Celebrity chef Jose Andres, who owns several restaurants in the capital, was among several high-profile critics of the effort. "So we are banning all meats?" Andres said in October. item.description: WASHINGTON — Democratic control of the U.S. Congress could make it harder for South Korea to acquire nuclear-powered submarines and limit President Donald Trump's ability to reach a deal with North Korea, even as he may seek another summit with leader Kim Jong-un, according to experts Wednesday. The assessments came after the Democratic Party scored a landslide victory in Tuesday's midterm elections, with the party poised to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, dealing a major political blow to Trump. item.title: Ex-Diddy prosecutor to lead Cornell gang rape investigation
item.description: NEW YORK — New York's attorney general on Wednesday named an ex-federal prosecutor who oversaw the criminal case against Sean "Diddy" Combs to lead an investigation into an alleged gang rape at Cornell University. The 2024 incident, as alleged in a graphic lawsuit filed last month, involved a female student being pressured to take ketamine, assaulted and raped by seven male students on campus. Cornell, an Ivy League institution in New York state, was widely accused of failing to properly punish the men involved, and the case sparked nationwide outrage. Attorney General Letitia James said that Jacqueline Kelly would lead a "fair and comprehensive investigation" into the alleged gang rape. "Jacqueline Kelly is a seasoned prosecutor who has overseen numerous cases from investigation through trial," James said. Kelly oversaw the 2025 conviction of Combs for prostitution-related crimes after a high-profile trial that detailed sexual marathons organized by the disgraced music producer. item.title: White House insists Trump is 'still your president' after midterm rout
item.description: WASHINGTON — Donald Trump is "still your president," the White House said Wednesday, a day after his Republican Party suffered sweeping losses in midterm elections seen as a referendum on his second term. The White House delivered the message in a post on X featuring a picture of a glaring Trump looming over the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office. "PSA: TRUMP IS STILL YOUR PRESIDENT," text superimposed on the image said, using the abbreviation for public service announcement. "Thank you for your attention to this matter," the post added, using a phrase Trump frequently employs in his social media messages. Opposition Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate on Tuesday, dealing a major blow to Trump and the Republican Party. The Democratic capture of Congress signals an end to Trump's stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to pass legislation, launch investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his appointments. item.title: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks after Trump election rout
item.description: TEHRAN — Iran's supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if the U.S. resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes of a policy shift in Washington after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. Trump has recently threatened to renew the war against Iran amid similar rhetoric from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but on Tuesday he suffered a resounding defeat in polls that will strip his Republicans of control over Congress. The results could constrain Trump's ability to enact his agenda, though the president retains the power to order new strikes. "Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken," Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement Wednesday. He also warned that if the United States did choose further military action, the scope of the war would widen, without elaborating. K

item.title: Democrats usher in new era with resounding sweep of the House and the Senate
item.description: WASHINGTON — Democrats are riding their sweep of Congress into a new era, eager to meet voter demands for change with plans to tackle high costs of living and confront President Donald Trump's final years in the White House. In a nationwide romp, Democrats ousted Republicans from coast to coast, with many surprising places in between, as voters rejected the president’s party for the promise of something different for the country. Their majorities will be padded by wide margins in both the House and the Senate. The results set up a divided government, with Congress poised to reassert itself as a coequal branch ready to challenge Trump and reverse course after two years of unified GOP control. “We hear you,” said House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who would make history as the first Black speaker of the House if his colleagues elect him to the job when the new Congress begins on Jan. 3, 2027. “We're going to work hard to deliver on the dramatic change that you deserve,” he said. item.title: Why Europe's supermarket fridges were easy targets
item.description: BRUGES, Belgium — Hackers who cranked up fridge temperatures at supermarkets across Europe may have gained access through public internet-connected systems protected by default passwords or outdated software, a cybersecurity expert said. The second cyberattack in three weeks hit fridge systems at supermarket chains including Carrefour and Delhaize in Belgium, and ICA and Coop in Sweden, forcing retailers to discard spoiled food and raising concerns about food security. Three blood banks in France were also hit. Authorities have not publicly disclosed how the attackers gained access, and no perpetrator has been identified. Laurens Singier, an ethical hacker and researcher at Cyber 3 Lab, part of Howest University of Applied Sciences in Bruges, Belgium, said internet-connected systems which can be accessible remotely often have weak protections. "In this case, the weak point was mainly putting those devices on the public internet. They shouldn't even be there," he said, speaking from a lab full of servers and systems similar to those that could control supermarket store fridges. A common

item.title: US stocks surge, Brent oil's price drops below $95 per barrel
item.description: NEW YORK — U.S. stocks are soaring Wednesday after President Donald Trump’s party lost its sole control of Washington in the midterm elections. Stocks generally do well in the months following any midterm U.S. election, regardless of who wins, and the S&P 500 jumped 1.8 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 1,524 points, or 2.9 percent, as of noon Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 2.1 percent higher. Stocks of solar-power companies, dollar stores and hospital owners helped lead the way as Wall Street tried to sort the winners from losers following the widespread losses for Republicans. Investors, meanwhile, see risks ahead for Trump’s social-media company, the artificial-intelligence industry and businesses owned by Elon Musk, who donated heavily to Republicans. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil fell below $100 for the first time in nearly a month. Vice President JD Vance blamed the war with Iran, which caused a spike in oil prices, for Republicans’ midterm losses. Strategists along Wall Street had been urging investors not to get swept up in the elect

item.title: From 'Unemployed Lee Sedol' to 'Dead-End Job,' labor becomes content
item.description: As concerns grow that artificial intelligence (AI) could replace humans in the workplace, the broadcasting industry is turning its attention to labor. A growing number of programs are exploring the subject, ranging from dramas set in workplaces and variety shows examining the realities of office workers to observational programs that put life without work front and center. Released on Netflix on Friday, the series “Dead-End Job” is a horror comedy about a young man named Hyuk-jun, who is sent into nightmarish workplaces after signing up with a bizarre employment agency that offers nothing but seemingly lucrative part-time jobs, starting at 50 times the standard hourly wage. Combining the familiar reality of part-time work with surreal mysteries and horror elements, the series offers an unconventional genre experience. item.title: Korean celebrities reveal painful school bullying experiences
item.description: Korean television personality Lee Hye-sung has opened up about her painful experience of being bullied during her school years, drawing renewed attention to similar revelations by celebrities including actor Park Seo-joon, singer Sung Si-kyung and travel YouTuber KwakTube. On Friday, Lee discussed the bestselling self-help book "The Courage to Be Disliked" on her YouTube channel, Lee Hye-sung's 1% Book Club, offering advice to people struggling with school bullying and social exclusion. "If you think school is the only community where you belong, it can be incredibly painful when you're bullied or can't make friends," Lee said. "I've been through it myself." Reflecting on her middle school years, Lee said she had struggled to see beyond the difficult circumstances she faced at the time. "When I was younger, in middle school, I couldn't think that way. There wasn't an adult around who could tell me something like that, either," she said. "That's why the situation was so incredibly painful and difficult." item.title: "They Have Eyes": How Trump's Corruption Became a Top Concern for Midterm Voters
item.source:markdown:
Democrats regained control of both the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s historic midterm elections, a comeback fueled largely by voter anger over high prices and the war on Iran. But surveys also found that corruption was a major concern, with 76% of voters telling a Harris poll that elected officials care more about enriching themselves than improving the economy for ordinary people. A separate Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 63% of Americans considered it inappropriate for Trump and his family to profit from cryptocurrency, while 69% said his private business interests influence his decisions as president.
“If this election was about corruption and cost, then this next Congress needs to be focused on accountability and affordability,” says Donald Sherman, the president and CEO of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, or CREW.
“Congress needs to do oversight not just on the administration’s corruption, not just on the president’s profiteering, but also on corporate America, what they have gotten out of engaging in the president’s pay-to-play environment, how corporate America and the outside influence of money in our political system has undermined the public voice in our policy discussions.”
item.author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)

item.title: First Gen Z Congresswoman: DSA's Melat Kiros on Corruption, Medicare for All & Israel
item.description:
The Democratic Socialists of America made major gains in this year’s U.S. midterms, electing not just the largest-ever socialist bloc to Congress, but also winning dozens of races at the state, county and municipal levels. Democracy Now! spoke with Congressmember-elect Melat Kiros on election night following her victory in Denver, Colorado. She identified Medicare for All as her top priority and said progressives must lay the groundwork “so that in ’29, when we have the House, the Senate and the White House, we can sign it into law on day one.”

Kiros is a 29-year-old Ethiopian immigrant and lawyer. In 2023, Kiros wrote an open letter about the danger of conflating antisemitism and criticism of Israel, for which she was fired by her law firm. She won a major upset in the Democratic primary earlier this year against longtime incumbent Congressmember Diana DeGette.

item.title: The Country Says "No" to Trump: Not Just Congress, the Blue Tsunami Flips Statehouses Across U.S.
item.description:
We examine the results of Tuesday’s historic U.S. midterm elections with Daniel Nichanian, editor-in-chief of Bolts. In addition to taking back the House and Senate, Democrats also made major gains at the state level and will control a majority of governorships for the first time in 16 years. Democrats also flipped 12 state legislative chambers.

“The size of the wins for Democrats in statewide races was wild,” says Nichanian. He identifies protecting abortion access, bolstering unions and ending police cooperation with ICE as some of the priorities Democrats are likely to pursue.

item.title: SK Group chairman to chair board of SK hynix's US AI arm
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won will chair the board of HYAICO, the U.S.-based artificial intelligence (AI) investment arm of SK hynix, according to documents filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The filing, made public Wednesday local time, identified the company as HYAICO, formerly known by its tentative name AI, which SK hynix announced in January with plans to invest up to $10 billion. SK hynix earlier said the new arm would help "accelerate AI advancement in global markets" and "find new AI growth engines." The new arm will be launched by restructuring SK hynix's existing U.S. arm, SK hynix NAND Product Solutions, also known as Solidigm. The chipmaker will instead set up a separate subsidiary called Solidigm to retain the brand name. Other current and former SK Group executives, meanwhile, will join Chey on HYAICO's board, and SK hynix President Song Hyun-jong will serve as HYAICO's chief executive.

item.title: Iran supreme leader says those expecting US policy shift 'seriously mistaken'
item.description: TEHRAN — Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Wednesday that anyone expecting a shift in U.S. policy was "seriously mistaken," hours after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. "Those who still harbor even the slightest hope that the behavior of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the U.S. can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken," Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website. Democrats seized control of the U.S. Congress in Tuesday's midterms, reflecting anger over living costs, tariffs and the U.S. war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring. Khamenei's remarks come with diplomatic efforts underway to avert renewed fighting in the war, which broke out on February 28. U.S. and Israeli leaders have in recent days threatened to resume attacks against Iran. item.title: Trump's midterm drubbing demonstrates power of data-center opponents
item.description: Opponents of data centers were among the biggest winners of the Democrats' landslide wins in the U.S. midterm elections, pointing to a shifting public mood on artificial intelligence (AI) and, investors said, a possible slowdown of the boom that has propelled U.S. economic growth and stock markets. The size and breadth of the Democratic wave were still coming into focus. But in gubernatorial races in Texas and Georgia, Democrats who campaigned in part on a moratorium on data center development won offices that the party had not held for decades. Their victories hand political heft to the backlash against the projects, which are at the heart of the AI boom but are loud, thirsty for water, hungry for electricity and increasingly unpopular with their neighbors, investors said. Investors say the results are likely to usher in tougher regulation and could ripple across financial markets where AI stocks were falling on Wednesday; big bets have already started to wobble due to concerns about spending and overcapacity. item.title: Koh becomes 7th Korean American elected to US Congress; Strickland secures 4th term
item.description: Dan Koh became the seventh Korean American elected to the U.S. Congress after winning a House seat in Massachusetts in Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, while fellow Democrat and Korean American Marilyn Strickland secured her fourth House term. The AP called the race in Massachusetts' 6th congressional district for Koh over Republican Micah Quinney Jones. With 77 percent of the vote counted, Koh had secured 63.42 percent, comfortably ahead of Jones, who garnered 36.58 percent. A former White House official during former President Joe Biden's administration and Boston mayoral aide, Koh previously ran for Congress in another Massachusetts district in 2018 but lost in the Democratic primary. Koh, 41, whose father is Korean and mother is Lebanese, has family roots in South Korea's southern resort island of Jeju. His grandfather previously worked at the South Korean Embassy in Washington. item.title: DaouKiwoom-CJ consortium to sign deal to acquire JoongAng Ilbo this week
item.description: A consortium comprising CJ, Shinsegae and two other companies will sign a deal Thursday to acquire debt-laden South Korean newspaper publisher JoongAng Ilbo, the company said Wednesday. Under the deal, the DaouKiwoom-CJ consortium will purchase 520 billion won ($388 million) worth of new shares in JoongAng Ilbo, with Daou Technology, CJ, Shinsegae and Saramin contributing 36.5 percent, 35.7 percent, 14.1 percent and 13.7 percent, respectively. The agreement, set to be signed Thursday, would make the consortium JoongAng Ilbo's largest shareholder. item.description: In 2023, despite freezing inter-Korean relations and heightened cross-border tensions, North Korea proposed a joint UNESCO heritage listing for taekwondo — only for the South Korean government to sit on the offer and miss a crucial window, according to a key advocacy leader. Choi Jae-chun, head of the KOREA Taekwondo UNESCO Promotion Committee, revealed Wednesday that Pyongyang suggested a collaborative inscription modeled after the successful joint 2018 UNESCO registration of "ssireum," traditional Korean wrestling. However, the lack of response from the Yoon Suk Yeol administration allowed North Korea to press ahead with a standalone application that is nearing final approval next month, raising fears that Seoul is ceding historical leadership over its national martial art. "In 2023, North Korea reached out to me," Choi said. item.description: Hoban Group has become the largest shareholder of Hanjin KAL, overtaking Hanjin Group Chairman Cho Won-tae and his related parties, according to a regulatory filing Wednesday, marking a significant shift in the ownership structure of the holding company behind Korean Air. item.title: Doctor injured in stabbing attack at hospital in western Seoul
item.description: A man stabbed and injured a doctor at a major hospital in western Seoul, police said Wednesday, adding that they are investigating the motive for the attack. The Seodaemun Police Station said it apprehended the man presumed to be in his 50s on suspicion of aggravated assault after he allegedly stabbed a psychiatry professor with a knife at Severance Hospital at around 4:30 p.m. The doctor sustained a wound measuring 5 centimeters and was taken to an emergency room for treatment. According to sources, the suspect was not a patient waiting for medical treatment at the hospital. Police are investigating the exact motive behind the suspect's attack.

item.description: Every two seconds, someone somewhere in the world buys a Laneige Lip Sleeping Mask. The small pink jar has become one of the best-known products of the K-beauty boom. How did a country that only a few generations ago had a handful of basic beauty creams become one of the world's top cosmetics exporters? Looking at Amorepacific R&I center's researcher, we explored story behind the lip mask, and the industry around it. The Lip Sleeping Mask is a favorite not only in Korea but also across North America and Europe. It has become a fixture at Sephora, where it ranks among the best-reviewed lip treatments. Shoppers in the U.S. and Canada have turned it into a cult favorite. One reason for that rise starts in Korea itself: Korean shoppers are known for reading ingredient lists, comparing reviews and switching brands quickly when something better comes along. item.title: From T-shirts to padded jackets: Why Korea's October weather swung so wildly
item.description: Koreans went from wearing short sleeves to pulling out padded winter jackets last month as temperatures swung dramatically between summer-like heat and early winter chills. The reason, meteorologists say, was a massive high-pressure system thousands of kilometers away over Russia's Ural Mountains. The atmospheric phenomenon, known as "Ural blocking," disrupted the usual flow of weather systems, allowing cold Arctic air to surge south toward the Korean Peninsula. Scientists say rapid warming in the Arctic may have helped intensify the disruption by weakening the jet stream that normally helps contain frigid air in northern latitudes. The Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) released its analysis of October's climate conditions on Wednesday, identifying extreme temperature variability as the month's defining characteristic. The difference between the warmest and coldest daily average temperatures nationwide reached 14 degrees Celsius, the fourth-largest October fluctuation on record. The average temperature stood at 22.1 degrees on Oct. 12 before plunging to 8.1 degrees on Oct. 28. Se

item.description: President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday voiced the need to revise what he described as the outdated Constitution, but said the revision should be led by the National Assembly through bipartisan efforts. Lee made the remarks at a lunch meeting at Cheong Wa Dae with the leadership of the Parliamentarian's Society, an association of former lawmakers, presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said. "Given the contemporary environment, the current Constitution is somehow like a cloth that does not fit contemporary society," the president was quoted as saying. He voiced the need to revise the Constitution but noted a constitutional revision led by the president may not be welcomed by the public, according to Kang. The president also highlighted the "high barrier" posed by the required consent of two-thirds of lawmakers to revise the Constitution, stressing that the most desirable way would be for the National Assembly to revise the Constitution through a bipartisan agreement. item.title: Korea experiences 5th warmest Oct. this year
item.description: Korea's average temperature reached 15.8 C last month, 1.5 C higher than the average for October, marking the fifth warmest October since 1973, the state weather agency said Wednesday. Korea saw unusually high temperatures from Oct. 10-13 as warm air moved in from the south, with Seoul's daily high reaching 30.1 C on Oct. 12, the highest October temperature since modern weather observation began in 1907, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA). Such high temperatures pushed the month's average up to 15.8 C, compared with the average temperature of 14.3 C from 1991 to 2022. This marks the fifth-highest nationwide mean temperature recorded for October since 1973 when weather observation networks were expanded to the entire nation. Temperatures also fluctuated sharply throughout the month as cold and warm air masses alternately flowed over the peninsula, driven by smooth atmospheric flows moving from west to east in the mid-latitudes. item.description: ULSAN — “Chae-a, do you like drawing?” “Yes!” “You won an award for your drawing. What did you do with your picture at school?” “I showed it off.” “How did you feel when you showed it to everyone?” “Happy. Excited.” The eight-year-old's answers were brief, but her drawings were filled with endless stories. Jang Chae-a, 8, a second-grader at Samdong Elementary School in Ulsan, won the gold prize in the 8-10 age category at the 2026 International Youth Art Contest (IYAC), a global competition for children and teenagers. She met with the Hankook Ilbo on Oct. 29 in Ulsan. Chae-a, who is on the autism spectrum, has difficulty expressing her thoughts spontaneously through speech. item.title: Regulator finalizes $276 mil. penalties on banks, securities firms over mis-selling of HK-tied derivatives
item.description: Seven banks and six securities firms were slapped with a combined 370 billion won ($276 million) in penalties by the financial regulator Wednesday over their mis-selling of equity-linked securities (ELS) products tracking Hong Kong's H Index. The amount is a sharp cut from the initial 1.4 trillion-won fine on the five lenders — KB Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Hana Bank, NH Nonghyup and SC Korea — which had already suffered massive losses as they had compensated customers over the mishap, according to the Financial Services Commission (FSC). Seoul's financial regulator finalized the penalty after ordering the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), the country's financial watchdog, to further review some legal issues. Earlier, the FSS had proposed a 600 billion-won penalty on the banks. The regulator imposed 361 billion won in penalties on the seven lenders. Banks and brokerages had sold a combined 19.3 trillion won worth of ELS products, tracking Hong Kong's H index since 2021, according to earlier data from the watchdog. item.title: Korean actors take on fictional fantasy monarchy in 'The Remarried Empress'
item.description: “I accept the divorce. And I request approval to remarry.” Korean actors portray a palace romance set in an imaginary empire in an unspecified time and place, where love and betrayal intertwine with power and desire in the Disney+ original series “The Remarried Empress.” Released Tuesday, the series is based on a hit web novel turned webtoon. The series opens the door to live-action adaptations of Korean romantic fantasy works. Can the bold experiment push genre boundaries and expand storytelling horizons? In Korea, the romantic fantasy genre typically combines fantasy elements with an imaginary aristocratic society reminiscent of medieval Europe. This has made live-action adaptations particularly challenging. When KBS adapted the web novel “The First Night With the Duke” into a drama, it relocated the story to the Joseon era and gave its characters Korean names to make the setting more familiar to viewers. “The Remarried Empress,” however, takes a different approach, focusing on recreating the original fantasy world on screen. item.title: Korea will not be affected by NASA's Swift telescope crashing back to earth: KASA
item.description: A defunct NASA telescope is expected to fall back to Earth on Wednesday evening, but it is highly unlikely the observatory will crash near the Korean Peninsula, Korea's space agency said. The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, also known as the Swift telescope, is projected to reenter the Earth's atmosphere at around 8:46 p.m., the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) said, citing an analysis from the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI). The margin of error is two hours, it added. Launched in 2004, the 1.5-ton telescope had been operating for the past 22 years on its mission to observe high-energy gamma-ray bursts. The observatory, however, had been slowly falling out of orbit, and NASA in July attempted to send a private satellite to bump the telescope so it can regain some altitude, but the plan failed. Eventually, the telescope had reached the point of no return and was shut down on Oct. 20. item.title: Korea Zinc Q3 net income soars 218.6% to $167.9 mil.
item.description: Korea Zinc Inc. on Wednesday reported its third-quarter net income of 225.4 billion won ($167.9 million), a surge of 218.6 percent from a year earlier. Operating profit for the July-September period, however, stood at 141.7 billion won, down 48.2 percent from a year ago, the company that produces various metals and engages in renewable-related businesses said in a regulatory filing. Sales rose 46.3 percent to 6.08 trillion won. The earnings fell short of market expectations. The average estimate of net profit by analysts stood at 271.5 billion won, according to a survey by Yonhap Infomax, the financial data firm of Yonhap News Agency.

item.description: A parliamentary subcommittee on Wednesday approved a bill calling for a special counsel to investigate allegations of fabricated indictments under the previous administration, including those involving President Lee Jae Myung. The subcommittee of the National Assembly's legislation and judiciary committee, led by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), passed the bill seeking an independent probe into allegations that prosecutors under the previous Yoon Suk Yeol administration had fabricated evidence to indict then opposition leader Lee. item.title: Korea draws record $2 bil. foreign investment pledges in AI, semiconductors
item.description: Korea secured a record $2 billion in foreign investment pledges from seven global companies, primarily in semiconductors, advanced materials and energy industry, as the government seeks to position the country as a key investment destination amid growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and advanced manufacturing. The Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) said the pledges were announced at its annual Invest Korea Summit 2026, a three-day investment promotion event jointly hosted by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources, which opened in Seoul on Wednesday. The event brought together 267 foreign investors and companies, along with around 2,000 business officials globally. The investment commitments mark the largest amount ever secured at the annual summit in its 22-year history, with about 97 percent of the pledged funds earmarked for regions outside the Seoul metropolitan area. item.title: Lee set to launch new YouTube program to communicate with public
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung will launch a YouTube program aimed at explaining his state administration to the public and answering people's questions, a presidential official said Wednesday. The first 30-minute episode of the new program, "President's Y," will be aired Thursday night on the president's YouTube channel, and new episodes will be released every two to three weeks, according to Lee's press secretary, Seong Ghi-hong. During the pre-filmed program, Lee plans to "voice his frank opinions in the language of the people in a comfortable atmosphere and answer questions from the public," Seong told a press briefing. The new program is part of Lee's efforts to communicate better with the public and provide more sufficient explanations of his thoughts and policies, the presidential official added.

item.title: Seoul stocks face fresh uncertainty as Democrats retake US Congress
item.description: Korean stocks face growing policy uncertainty after Democrats regained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the U.S. midterm elections, according to market analysts, Wednesday. They say obstacles to extending corporate tax cuts and the prospect of stricter oversight of Big Tech and artificial intelligence (AI) could fuel volatility in Korea’s tech-heavy stock market. However, sweeping policy changes remain unlikely given U.S. President Donald Trump’s veto power and ability to issue executive orders, the analysts said. Over the medium term, Korean stocks are expected to be driven more by returns on AI investment, semiconductor demand and foreign investor flows than by the election outcome itself. KOSPI closed slightly higher after a volatile session as investors assessed the implications of the Democrats’ victory. After rebounding 2.24 percent in the previous session, the benchmark opened at 5,786.13, up 137.34 points, or 2.43 percent, and climbed as high as 5,828.13, a gain of 3.17 percent. It then reversed course, falling as much as 4.02 percent to 5,421.

item.title: Democratic sweep in US midterms dims prospects for Trump-Kim summit, analysts say
item.description: The Democrats’ victory in both the House and Senate in Tuesday's (local time) U.S. midterm elections has made a summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un even less likely, analysts said Wednesday, though others argued that Trump’s tendency to shrug off political pressure means he may keep pursuing a meeting regardless. A Trump-Kim meeting had been floated as a possible diplomatic surprise around the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, scheduled for Nov. 18 and 19 in Shenzhen, China. The two leaders met three times during Trump’s first term from 2017 to 2021, but a fourth meeting was already in doubt before the elections, given Kim’s lukewarm response to renewed U.S. outreach. Some analysts said the prospect has also lost some of its appeal as a headline-grabbing event, with attention shifting to a possible U.S.-China-Russia summit in Shenzhen. item.title: Democratic midterm gains may fuel fresh trade uncertainty for Korea
item.description: Democratic gains in both chambers of the U.S. Congress in the midterm elections could expose Korea to fresh trade uncertainty, as experts warn that while such a shift would do little to curb U.S. President Donald Trump's tariff powers, it could complicate the implementation of Seoul's investment commitments and prompt him to intensify trade pressure. The $350 billion investment agreement between Seoul and Washington is unlikely to be overturned, as expanding U.S. manufacturing has bipartisan support. However, the political fallout from the Republican defeat could put pressure on Trump to demonstrate progress on his trade agenda, with Korea potentially facing renewed tariff threats, the experts said. "The tools used to exert tariff pressure are unlikely to change," said Jang Sang-sik, head of trade trend analysis at the Korea International Trade Association, referring to Section 232 and Section 301 of the U.S. trade law, which provide the administration with legal grounds to impose tariffs. item.title: Korean won to strengthen against dollar following Democrats' midterm sweep
item.description: The Korean won is expected to strengthen against the U.S. dollar after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, as political tensions in Washington and a potential sell-off in U.S. equities could weigh on the dollar, experts said Wednesday. Democratic control of Congress is expected to complicate U.S. President Donald Trump's efforts to advance his economic agenda, including tax cuts and expanded government spending, while giving lawmakers greater power to scrutinize his administration's policies. The prospect of a prolonged standoff between the White House and Congress could unsettle investors and undermine confidence in U.S. financial markets, said Shin Se-don, an economics professor at Sookmyung Women's University. "A fierce confrontation between Congress and the Trump administration will be inevitable. Trump's economic policy initiatives could face setbacks as Democrats step up opposition to the administration's policies, potentially slowing growth across the broader U.S. economy," Shin said. item.title: Imported vehicle sales jump 29.3% in Oct. on strong EV demand
item.description: Sales of imported vehicles in Korea rose a sharp 29.3 percent in October from a year earlier, driven by robust demand for electric vehicles (EVs), industry data showed Wednesday. New registrations increased to 31,117 units last month from 24,064 a year earlier, according to the Korea Automobile Importers & Distributors Association (KAIDA). The three top-selling imported cars were the Tesla Model Y Premium, Mercedes-Benz E200 and Tesla Model 3. The two Tesla models are manufactured in China for the Korean market, allowing the company to offer them at competitive prices. Tesla's sales more than doubled to 9,165 units last month from 4,350 a year earlier. However, its sales fell 25.9 percent from the previous month due to supply shortages, KAIDA said. The U.S. EV maker remained the best-selling imported passenger car brand in Korea for the ninth consecutive month, extending its run since February. item.title: Police arrest 80 high-risk offenders in relationship-based crime review
item.description: Police said Wednesday they have conducted a comprehensive review of about 44,000 cases involving relationship-based crime, such as stalking and domestic violence, and placed under custody 80 individuals identified as high-risk offenders. The 12-day review, which began Oct. 19, covered 44,540 cases, according to the Korean National Police Agency. They included 43,712 existing cases, such as those currently under investigation, individuals subject to high-risk monitoring, stalking reports that had previously been closed at the scene and cases involving ongoing safety measures. The police classified 5,068, or 32 percent, of the 15,840 cases currently under investigation as high-risk. Regarding high-risk offenders, police requested 376 arrest warrants, of which 80, or 21.3 percent, were issued by courts. They also requested 321 orders for the attachment of electronic monitoring devices, of which 104, or 32.4 percent, were approved by courts. item.title: Trump hand-picked Senate candidates. Republicans paid the price
item.description: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump asked voters to pretend he was on the ballot in the midterm elections and handpicked Republican candidates in some of the country's most consequential Senate races. By Tuesday night, voters had rejected them. Trump-backed candidates in South Carolina, North Carolina and Texas all lost, while the president's preferred pick trailed in early results in Michigan. The defeats handed Democrats control of the chamber and exposed the limits of Trump's political power. Trump has spent more than a decade reshaping the Republican Party around his MAGA movement, dictating primary matchups and pushing aside conservative figures he felt were insufficiently loyal or not aligned with his vision. Trump repeatedly favored loyalists and ideological allies over more established Republicans with stronger statewide networks and proven electoral track records, betting that his endorsement could overcome their political liabilities. Tuesday's results revealed he was unable to persuade the broader electorate to back his choices. One of the most stunning repudiations came in

item.title: More productive, attractive regions outside Seoul key to sustaining growth: OECD officials
item.description: Korea needs to boost productivity in regions outside the capital area and make them more attractive places to live as it seeks to sustain economic growth and address demographic challenges, officials at the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said Wednesday. Lamia Kamal-Chaoui, director of the Center for Entrepreneurship, SMEs, Regions and Cities at the Paris-based institution, said in an interview with Yonhap News Agency that the OECD has seen "something very interesting" in Korea. Despite the concentration of people and economic activity in the capital region, the country's regional gaps in GDP per capita are among the smallest in the OECD, she said. "Indeed, you have the largest concentration of the capital region across the OECD," Kamal-Chaoui said. "(But the economic growth of Korea came with) a level of regional disparities in terms of GDP per capita that is the lowest among the lowest in the OECD." item.title: HS Hyosung vice chair highlights private diplomacy at OECD anniversary dinner
item.description: HS Hyosung Vice Chairman Cho Hyun-sang has stepped up efforts to promote private-sector diplomacy as Korea marks the 30th anniversary of its membership in the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). Cho delivered congratulatory remarks at a dinner commemorating the anniversary, hosted by the Federation of Korean Industries (FKI) in Seoul Tuesday. He attended as a Korean board member of Business at OECD (BIAC). The event brought together around 80 participants, including OECD Deputy Secretary-General Frantisek Ruzicka, diplomatic representatives from 26 countries and Korean business leaders. They reviewed Korea's economic achievements over the past three decades and discussed ways to expand global economic cooperation. "Korea has reached a point where it can stand firmly on its own as an OECD member, marking a true milestone of ‘irip,’" Cho said, referring to the Confucian concept of becoming self-reliant at the age of 30. item.title: PM pledges to root out price-fixing practices
item.description: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook pledged Wednesday to root out price-fixing practices, saying the government has imposed more than 1.8 trillion won ($1.3 billion) in administrative fines this year alone on companies involved in collusion. Han made the remark in a post on X, saying stabilizing prices is an important responsibility of the government. "We will firmly safeguard the people's dining tables from price-fixing," she said. Noting the amount of administrative fines imposed this year for price-fixing of sugar, eggs, flour and starch sugars, Han said the penalties led to price drops of up to 26.5 percent for those items. "This means that companies had been placing a heavy burden on the people's dining tables," she said, promising to root out such collusion. "We will strengthen economic sanctions to ensure that no further profit can be gained through collusion."

item.title: Seoul's outdoor libraries top 10 mil. visitors, set to reopen in April
item.description: Seoul's outdoor libraries have drawn more than 10 million visits since their launch in 2022, turning public squares and urban waterways into popular reading spaces and drawing growing attention from overseas media and library professionals. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that this year's program attracted approximately 1.87 million visitors to three main locations — Seoul Plaza, Gwanghwamun Square and Cheonggye Stream — before closing for its winter break on Nov. 1. The cumulative figure of more than 10 million includes visitors to district-run and pop-up outdoor libraries since the initiative began. A satisfaction survey of 5,155 visitors found that 97 percent were satisfied with the program, while 97.4 percent said they intended to return and 97.8 percent said they would recommend it to others. The survey also found that 90.3 percent of respondents had actually read books during their visits, suggesting the spaces have become more than places to relax. item.title: Jeonbuk National University alumna appointed assistant professor at University of Central Florida
item.description: Song Seong-mi, an alumna of Jeonbuk National University’s Division of Biomedical Engineering, has been appointed assistant professor in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of Central Florida. Song enrolled in Jeonbuk National University in 2007, where she developed a strong foundation in engineering. In 2014, she began graduate studies in the university’s Department of Healthcare Engineering, gaining research experience in biomedical and rehabilitation engineering. She later earned a Ph.D. in motor neuroscience from Texas A&M University, further expanding her expertise. Jeonbuk National University said the appointment is significant as it marks an alumna’s transition from studying at the university at both undergraduate and graduate levels to pursuing an academic career at a U.S. university. It also demonstrates how interdisciplinary experience in engineering and health care can open up new career opportunities, serving as an inspiring example for students aspiring to become researchers in related fields. item.title: Seven Luck casino introduces 24-hour AI phone service in 4 languages
item.description: State-run casino operator Grand Korea Leisure (GKL) has introduced a 24-hour artificial intelligence (AI) telephone service at its Gangnam Coex branch, offering automated support in four languages — Korean, English, Chinese and Japanese — to streamline customer inquiries. The state-run casino operator said the AI call bot is the first system of its kind introduced in the industry and is designed to handle routine inquiries around the clock. Customers calling the branch can listen to an introductory message before asking questions in Korean or one of the three foreign languages, with the system responding in the language used. The AI service provides information about the casino's location, operating hours, parking facilities and admission requirements. Calls involving reservation checks or more detailed consultations are transferred to the appropriate staff members. GKL said it built a database of frequently asked questions during a trial operation conducted from June through September, using common customer inquiries to develop the system's responses. item.title: BMW Korea unveils facelifted 7 Series luxury sedan to take on Mercedes-Benz S-Class
item.description: BMW Korea unveiled its redesigned 7 Series luxury sedan, Wednesday, seeking to build on its growing presence in the higher-end market, as the flagship model gains ground rapidly against the long-dominant Mercedes-Benz Korea’s S-Class. The launch carries significance beyond the arrival of an updated model. The 7 Series has emerged as one of BMW Korea's key growth drivers, capitalizing on weakening demand for its archrival Mercedes-Benz S-Class in the large luxury sedan segment that BMW has traditionally struggled to dominate. The changing sales balance between the two models illustrates the shift. According to data from the Korea Automobile Importers & Distributors Association (KAIDA), the S-Class recorded 1,839 sales in Korea during the first half of this year, 1,238 fewer than the 7 Series' 3,077. The BMW luxury sedan also topped sales of imported large sedans in Korea in both 2024 and 2025, displacing the S-Class from its long-held position as the segment leader and dealing a blow to Mercedes-Benz's core identity as a super luxury carmaker.
